title: SpaceX Raptor 3 Vacuum
note: Raptor 3 Vacuum, as on Starship V3: the sea-level Raptor 3's chamber, powerhead and plumbing (raptor3_spec) with a large tube-wall bell. Frame: thrust axis z up, nozzle exit at z = 0; +x towards the turbopump.

sources.title: FAA, Starship/Super Heavy draft EA, Appendix G: Exhaust plume calculations (Sierra Engineering, 2019), Table 1
sources.note: The 2019 (Raptor 1-era) sea-level nozzle. Nothing newer is published; photo_cmp shows Raptor 3's bell the same size and shape (facts.bell_matches_faa).

thrust_tf.quote: vacuum engines produce 275 tf (606,000 lbf) up from 258 tf (568,000 lbf).

height_m.source: raptor3_spec (2.94 m) plus the longer bell (design_rao: 3.327 m against 1.526 m)

open_questions: Bell length and contour: design_rao's 80% bell (3.33 m), not measured; nothing published for any Raptor Vacuum found. A side photo would fix it.
Above the throat it is the sea-level Raptor 3 (raptor3_spec); the vacuum engine's own plumbing may differ.
Bell finish: sampled from photo_ship_underside, whose ship version isn't known.

exit.source: render_aft_b3: 2.45 m plus the 0.012 m wall either side

raptor_black.source: photo_cmp, the bell where no sky reflects: its lit left (2700-2760, 1900-2000) #343a45 and shaded right (3200-3260, 1900-2000) #212833, averaged. The cone above the bell reads lighter (#6b7688 at 2880-2930, 1330-1380) only where it faces the sky.

raptor_steel.source: photo_cmp, the top flange (2860-2960, 582-595) #5b646a and the gimbal cap (2920-2980, 420-460) #858d9f

exit_diameter.source: render_aft_b3, seen from below: the vacuum bells 155-162 px across where the skirt's open end (9 m) is 580 px; as specs/starship.json from_photos.engines.rvac_exit

throat_diameter.source: faa_plume: "Throat Radius (in) 4.362"; the vacuum engine's chamber and throat taken as the sea-level Raptor 3's (raptor3_spec)

length.source: design_rao: an 80% bell (0.8 x the 15-degree cone from the 0.1108 m throat to the 1.225 m exit, 4.158 m); not measured, no Raptor Vacuum length found

initial_angle_deg.source: faa_plume: "Tangency angle (deg) 32.0" (the sea-level nozzle's; same chamber and throat)

exit_angle_deg.source: design_rao: a typical exit angle for an 80% bell of area ratio about 120; not measured

wall.source: design_rao, design value: a thin tube-wall lip
